title: Minimizing Modality Gap from the Input Side: Your Speech LLM Can Be a Prosody-Aware Text LLM
claim: Prior systems bridge speech and text through lossy or decoupled designs; ours feeds prosody-aware text-like input and closes the gap with far less data.
layout: 2 parts: four architecture diagrams left-to-right, scatter plot at right
description: The left side shows four vertical block diagrams, each reading bottom to top. A speech waveform feeds a bottom encoder, then an LLM, then output tokens. Panel (a) is speech-only, (b) uses intermediate text, (c) is text-speech decoupled with a Talker module, and (d) is TextPro-SLM (ours). Panel (d) replaces the speech encoder with a cyan WhisperPro block that emits text tokens plus a purple prosody embedding, and it has an optional dashed Talker. Colored squares stand for text tokens (blue), speech tokens (green), speech embeddings (dashed green) and prosody embeddings (purple). A legend sits at the top left. The right side is a scatter plot of 100 minus modality gap against audio training hours on a log scale. A red star for Ours sits at the top left, with blue dots for the baselines below and to the right.
caption: Left: Comparison of the architectural designs used by prior SLMs and our approach. Right: Comparison of modality gap versus the amount of audio training data across different approaches.
abstract: Speech large language models (SLMs) are typically built from text large language model (TLM) checkpoints, yet they still suffer from a substantial modality gap. Prior work has mainly attempted to reduce this gap from the output side by making speech generation more text-like, but the gap remains. We argue that the key remaining bottleneck lies on the input side. We propose TextPro-SLM, an SLM that makes spoken input more closely resemble that of a prosody-aware text LLM. TextPro-SLM combines WhisperPro, a unified speech encoder that produces synchronized text tokens and prosody embeddings, with an LLM backbone trained to preserve the semantic capabilities of the original TLM while learning paralinguistic understanding. Experiments show that TextPro-SLM achieves the lowest modality gap among leading SLMs at both 3B and 7B scales, while also delivering strong overall performance on paralinguistic understanding tasks. These gains are achieved with only roughly 1,000 hours of LLM training audio, suggesting that reducing the modality gap from the input side is both effective and data-efficient. Code is available at https://github.com/dreamtheater123/TextPro-SLM
